basis.label: Hydronic/Water Circulating Pumps
basis.note: Same life for family and elderly properties. US multifamily housing. HUD's row covers hydronic circulating pumps of any mounting.

basis.title: Design standards: employer's requirements – Technical Manual (ER-DFE-XX-XX-T-X-0201, revision A-C01)
basis.label: Storage cylinders, valves and pumps: 20 years
basis.note: Printed page 245. Heating and cooling system pumps (cylinders and valves not mapped). Minimum life expectancy (design requirement) for DfE-funded school buildings. Minimum design requirements placed on contractors for school buildings, not observed replacement ages. Section 5.1.4 (sanitaryware) refers to CIBSE Guide M Appendix 12.A1 'in general'.

basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Pumps (final rule), 81 FR 4368, January 26, 2016
basis.by: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
basis.label: Equipment Lifetime: "The average across all equipment classes was 15 years"
basis.note: Printed page 4394. All-class average for commercial and industrial clean-water pumps; brine pumps are outside DOE scope (clean water only) so the brine-pump match is loose.

basis.title: General depreciation rates (IR265), July 2021
basis.by: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand
basis.label: Centrifugal pumps
basis.note: Printed page 51. Pumping sets (where not industry specified). End-suction base-mounted pumps are centrifugal pumps. Printed DV 20%, SL 13.5%. Tax depreciation lives set by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue for New Zealand income tax, not engineering or asset-management lives; they are banded and often short (e.g. reticulation piping 25 years). The July 2021 edition was the newest PDF reachable; the online Depreciation Rate Finder may hold later determinations.

open_questions: Every source here is a published planning, design or accounting life. None is observed replacement data.
